besluite.fout: The particle 'oop' of the separable verb is split off before the prepositional phrase, which reads as loose spoken order in written text.
besluite.rede: Placing 'oop' at the end of the clause is the standard written Afrikaans order and the meaning (the shell splits on one side) is unchanged.
'Dan' already reads naturally as 'in that case' here, and 'So' would repeat the 'So' that opens the block's last sentence ('So word die stam lank en swak').

'n Hele klomp sade' is natural plain Afrikaans for a Grade 4 reader that stresses how many seeds there are, and the following 'n hele nuwe plant' contrasts with it rather than jarring; 'baie' only reads differently.
